title: Priv EKS control plane Terraform: warm-boot optimizer and staged upgrade flow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem context:
As Private (VPC) customers increase, full control-plane reprovisioning during routine upgrades or environment restores is the dominant source of long tail downtime and incurring unnecessary billable work. Traditional 'destroy-and-recreate' or heavyweight replacement strategies create customer-facing jitter, extended reconciliation times, and frequent post-upgrade remediation work.

Objective:
Deliver a Terraform module and accompanying orchestration patterns that enable 'warm-boot' EKS control-plane provisioning: reuse compatible persisted resources, perform staged upgrades with health gating, and provide automated reconciliation/repair hooks to minimize interruption and operator toil. The module should be idempotent, observable, and compatible with cross-account KMS and VPC peering patterns used by Private deployments.

What this ticket delivers:
- A terraform module (registry-style) exposing a warm_boot_enabled boolean and fine-grained controls (preflight_checks, fastpath_allowlist, staged_rollout_window).
- Preflight validators that run in CI and at apply-time (API reachability, KMS key policy checks, nodegroup compatibility matrix).
- A staged upgrade runner pattern: stage 0 (lightweight drift fix), stage 1 (control-plane component patch), stage 2 (configuration migration), each with programmable health gates and auto-rollback windows.
- Reconciliation and repair hooks that can invoke a limited set of terraform apply fixes or a lightweight operator to fix known drift classes (subnet tags, security-group rules, EBS encryption settings).
- Telemetry hooks (Prometheus metrics + structured logs) and tracing labels to attribute latency and failures to module phases.

Trade-offs and constraints considered:
- Complexity vs safety: the warm-boot path reduces downtime but adds subtle state checks; we avoid speculative in-place edits for large-schema migrations and require an opt-in migration plan when API-breaking changes are detected.
- Terraform state drift: we prefer reconciliation actions that are idempotent and small; avoid executing arbitrary imperative scripts during apply unless gated behind approval.
- Cross-account KMS: validating and patching key policies requires elevated privileges; module supports a 'dry-run' validation mode and emits remediation hints instead of automatic policy edits unless customer enablement flag is set.
- Testing surface: extensive integration tests against a small fleet of test clusters will be provided; however, some edge cases (region-specific resource quotas) will remain manual in early rollouts.

Success criteria:
- Module can perform a warm-boot cluster upgrade in under 15 minutes (common path) for 90% of test fixtures compared to baseline cold replacement of >45 minutes.
- Automated staged upgrade completes with zero manual restoration steps for 95% of synthetic upgrade tests.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Terraform module published to internal registry with versions >= v0.1.0 and clear upgrade notes.
2) CI integration tests demonstrating staged upgrade flow passing in lab environment (see links).
3) Runbook and playbook added to playbooks.redwood.ai covering rollback, telemetry triage, and customer communication template.
4) Security review completed and KMS cross-account remediation flow documented.
tasks: Design RFC for warm-boot lifecycle and staged rollout phases
Implement terraform module skeleton with warm_boot_enabled flag and feature gates
Add preflight validators (KMS, subnet/tagging, API reachability) as terraform data checks + CI scripts
Implement staged rollout orchestration (controller script + terraform orchestration wrapper)
Wire telemetry hooks into provisioning phases and emit Prometheus metrics
Write integration tests and stress scenarios (slow K8s API, partial drift, quota failures)
Author runbook and upgrade communications template
Open PR and run security review; iterate on feedback
comments: 2026-03-05 | Aisha Patel: Created ticket after sprint planning. Initial RFC sketch uploaded to Confluence (link above). Goal is to reduce upgrade time and improve observability during Private control-plane changes.

2026-03-07 | Diego Morales: Spike results: warm-boot reduced control-plane reconciliation on our small fixtures by ~3x when only tag/drift fixes required. Captured scripts and sample tf state diff in PR #421.
2026-03-09 | Security (Marta Ivanov): Requested more detail around KMS policy changes — prefer dry-run remediation + explicit customer opt-in. Marked security_review_required.
2026-03-10 | Diego Morales: Added preflight dry-run output and remediation hints to module. Updated acceptance criteria to include documented remediation flow.

2026-03-12 | QA (Liam Zhou): Integration tests added to CI pipeline. Found a race where subnet tag propagation lag caused a transient health gate failure; added a configurable retry backoff to staged runner.
